items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S326

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to enact the "New York state municipal separate stormwater
sewer system mandate relief act of 2017"; to enact the "New York state
stormwater management financing act of 2017"; and to provide for the
allocation of monies received by the state from any settlement with
Deutsche Bank (Subpart A); to direct the environmental facilities
corporation to provide financial assistance payments in support of
municipal stormwater management projects (Subpart B)(Part A); to make
an appropriation for the purposes of the New York state stormwater
management financing act of 2017 (Part B); to amend the public
authorities law, in relation to the drinking water revolving fund of
the environmental facilities corporation; to amend the state finance
law, in relation to establishing the drinking water program management
and administration fund; and to repeal section 97-ddd of the state
finance law relating to the drinking water program management and
administration fund (Part C); to amend the soil and water conservation
districts law, the town law, the administrative code of the city of
New York and the general municipal law, in relation to state aid for
watershed protection (Part D); to amend the environmental conservation
law, in relation to requiring consideration of a municipality's
financial capabilities and the affordability of control options when
issuing permits for wet weather discharges from sanitary sewers; and
to amend the public health law, in relation to eligibility for funding
from the drinking water revolving fund (Part E); and to amend the
general municipal law, the general city law, the county law and the
village law, in relation to the protection and restoration of
groundwater, surface waters and drinking water quality (Part F)

 PURPOSE :

This bill enacts the "New York State Municipal Separate Stormwater
Sewer System Mandate Relief Act of 2017" and the "New York State
Stormwater Management Financing Act of 2017".

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one creates the "New York State Municipal Separate Stormwater
Sewer System Mandate Relief Act of 2017".

Part A of the legislation creates the "New York State Stormwater
Management Financing Act of 2017" in two sub parts. Section 1 of
Subpart A captures the settlement funds received by New York State
from Deutsche Bank and directs their use to finance water projects
referred to in section 1045-b of the public authorities law or
non-agricultural nonpoint source abatement and control projects as
referred in section 17-1409 of the environmental conservation law.

Section 2 establishes the effective date for Subpart A.

Subpart B lays out the "New York State Stormwater Management Financing
Act of 2017". Section one provides definitions that identify
applicable projects as set forth in section 17-1403-of environmental
conservation law and as defined in paragraphs a, b, c and e of
subdivision four (4) of section 1160 of the public health law.
Section two caps grants to municipalities from the environmental
facilities corporation through this act to no more than ten million
dollars in a single fiscal year for storm water management projects.
Projects will include: SPEDES upgrades to existing sewage treatment
works; new sewage treatment works or community septic systems and
related infrastructure; sewer extensions; stormwater retrofits to
address existing stormwater runoff concerns; for the improvement of
sand and salt storage facilities; stream corridor protections; water
quality projects; rehabilitation or replacement of failing subsurface
sewage treatment systems and sewerage collection systems. This subpart
will take effect immediately and includes a severability clause.

Part B allocates the sum of six hundred million dollars to the
department of environmental conservation aid to localities budget to
fund the "New York State Stormwater Management Financing Act of 2017".
Funds shall be distributed up to two hundred million a year over a
three-year period.

Part C, section one directs the funds to the drinking water revolving
fund for use pursuant to the "New York State Stormwater Management
Financing Act of 2017". Section two renumbers section 97-ddd to 99-x
and adds projects from the New York state municipal separate
stormwater sewer system mandate relief act of 2017 as a permissible
expense of the fund. This subpart takes effect immediately.

Part D amends section 11-a of the soil and water conservation
districts law; section 198 of the town law; section 24-501 of the
administrative code of the city of New York; and section 119-c of the
general municipal law to identify the municipalities, soil and water
conservation districts and town watershed improvement districts that
are eligible to receive funding under the "New York State Stormwater
Management Financing Act of 2017". Part D, section five includes a
severability clause and the provisions of Part D takes effect
immediately.

Part E adds new section 17-0709 to the environmental conservation law
to require the commissioner of the department of environmental
conservation to give consideration where allowable to multiple factors
prior to issuing a SPDES permit including: a community's financial
ability to secure necessary funding; the affordability of control
options; an evaluation of the effectiveness and affordability of
control technologies; the promotion of green infrastructure; the
reduction of economic impacts on regulated entities, other state and
local government entities, and residents; allowance for reasonable
accommodations for entities when inflexible standards and fines would
impose a disproportionate financial hardship in light of the
environmental benefits to be gained, giving preference, when proposed
by a committee, to control options that meet presumption approach
performance criteria and demonstrate significant pollution reduction
rather than mandating specific designs; allowance of adequate time and
flexibility for implementation schedules when justified by a clear
environmental benefit, a community's ability to raise or secure
adequate funds, an analysis concluding that the costs of a shorter
implementation schedule outweigh the benefits of faster
implementation, or other facts; and factors set forth in the United
States Environmental Protection Agency's "Combined Sewer Overflow
Control Policy" that may ease the cost burdens of implementing
long-term control plans, including but not limited to small system
considerations, the attainability of water quality standards, and the
development of wet weather standards.

Section two of Part E amends section 1161 of the public health law to
include stormwater best practices, including source and nonpoint
source control measures, technical and environmental feasibility,
benefits, costs and cost effectiveness, the ability for a municipality
to pay and the affordability of control options when determining
eligibility and priority projects in the drinking water revolving
fund. Part E shall take effect immediately.

Part F amends multiple sections of law to enable counties, villages
and cities to create stormwater utilities or joint watershed
improvement districts that apply for funding via the "New York State
Stormwater Management Financing Act of 2017".

 JUSTIFICATION :
This legislation seeks to address a significant unfunded mandate
through the creation of a new financing program subsidized by
settlement funds received by New York State that will assist
municipalities with the costly Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System
(MS4) mandate. This legislation will provide municipalities with
flexibility and financing when achieving their clean water goals and
providing wet weather improvements.

In New York, the State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
is charged with general permitting authority via the Federal Clean
Water Act for the MS4 program. At this point, the determination of
compliance has been made with little consideration to the county and
local municipalities' ability to pay for the infrastructure upgrades
necessary to reduce pollutants in the waterways. Municipalities are
saddled with the burden of meeting the MS4 mandate without proper
financing, and the added scrutiny of taxpayers as they seek to remain
under the Real Property Tax Cap.

As such, many municipalities are forced to balance their fiduciary
responsibilities to their water and sewer ratepayers against the high
costs associated with meeting the MS4 mandates. Therefore, these
projects remain incomplete.

Along with a financing program, this legislation implements
recommendations by the United States Conference of Mayors to require
DEC to consider a municipality's ability to fund required
infrastructure modifications required under MS4.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-2016: S.5422A - Referred to Finance

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Allocates $600 million in settlement funds.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately provided, however, that the
applicable effective date of Parts A through F of this act shall be as
specifically set forth in the last section of such Parts.

summary: Enacts the " New York state separate stormwater sewer system mandate relief act of 2017"; appropriates $600,000,000 therefor; provides that moneys received from any settlement with Deutsche Bank shall be used to fund such appropriation; directs the environmental facilities corporation to fund municipal stormwater management projects; establishes a new drinking water program management and administration fund; provides state aid for watershed protection; requires the commissioner of environmental conservation to consider a municipality's financial capabilities and the affordability of control options during the issuance of permits for wet weather discharges from sanitary sewers; authorizes use of the drinking water revolving fund for stormwater best management practices; provides for the municipal protection and restoration of groundwater, surface waters and drinking water quality.
